query: The neurotransmitter glutamate initiates phasic postsynaptic currents following its release from synaptic vesicles and binding to ionotropic postsynaptic receptors. Glutamate is then cleared within milliseconds from the synaptic cleft by diffusion and the activity of excitatory amino acid transporters (EAATs). Rapid glutamate removal is essential to maintain brief and reliable transmission. By contrast, unipolar brush cells (UBCs) of the cerebellar cortex transform brief mossy fiber (MF) excitation into a prolonged postsynaptic current due to the persistence of glutamate in the synapse for hundreds of milliseconds after synaptic release (Lu et al., 2017; Rossi et al., 1995).
matched_segment: The neurotransmitter glutamate initiates phasic postsynaptic currents following its release from synaptic vesicles and binding to ionotropic postsynaptic receptors. By contrast, unipolar brush cells (UBCs) of the cerebellar cortex transform brief mossy fiber (MF) excitation into a prolonged postsynaptic current due to the persistence of glutamate in the synapse for hundreds of milliseconds after synaptic release (Lu et al., 2017; Rossi et al., 1995).
